# @sidestep/auth

> A [sidestep](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sidestep/core) package implementing
> Xano's quick-start authentication (`auth/signup`, `auth/login`, `auth/me`, plus
> the `user`, `account`, and `event_log` tables and an event-log function),
> recreated as typed sidestep defs you register into a workspace and version
> behind npm. It is also the **reference sidestep extension package**.

A sidestep extension package exports plain, typed def objects (the factories
`table()`, `query()`, `defineFunction()`, `apiGroup()` are pure identity
functions). The *consumer's* `Xano` instance does all registration and encoding
via `export()`. This package pins no guids, and no canonical unless you pass one
to `registerAuth` — otherwise identity comes from the consuming project's
`xano.lock`, or falls back to `md5("<kind>:<name>")`.

## Install

```bash
npm install @sidestep/auth @sidestep/core
```

`@sidestep/core` is a `>=3.9.25 <5.0.0` peer dependency — install the current
stable release. Built and tested against 4.1.2. The golden-bundle test in this
package is the peer-drift tripwire: if a core upgrade changes encoding, it fails
here before consumers are affected (for the installed version — the rest of the
range is declared, not CI-verified). The floor is 3.9.25, not the tested version:
it is the oldest core whose *types* this package needs (`auth/me`'s response is
derived from its stack, which needs core's miss-to-null handling for `db.get`).
It is verified, not asserted — against this same source, 3.9.25 typechecks clean
and the whole suite passes except the golden fixture, which tracks the installed
core's encoding rather than the defs.

The range deliberately spans a major rather than using a caret. sidestep 4.0.0
broke only the CLI's deploy surface (`sandbox deploy` → `deploy` + ephemeral
environments, `release`, `ephemeral`); the def-authoring API is untouched and no
4.x type is load-bearing here, so both 3.9.x and 4.x consumers are supported.
The defs themselves encode byte-identically all the way back to the 3.0.0 build
— the one bundle difference in 4.x is core's own addition of a name-derived
`guid` on the workspace object, so the committed fixture matches every 4.x core
and differs from a 3.9.x one by exactly that field.

## Quickstart

```ts
// xano/index.ts
import { workspace } from "@sidestep/core";
import { registerAuth } from "@sidestep/auth";

// Pin `canonical` to make getPath() resolve client-side with no lock file;
// omit the options object to leave the canonical to the consumer's xano.lock.
export default registerAuth(workspace("my-app"), { canonical: "authn" });
```

```bash
npx sidestep export   # → importable workspace bundle
```

## Exports

- `registerAuth(xano, opts?)` — one-call install of the full set; returns the
  instance for chaining. Idempotency-guarded (throws on a second call per
  instance). `opts.canonical` pins the Authentication group's URL segment (see
  the getPath note below); omit it to leave identity to the consumer's lock.
- Tables: `userTable` (auth table), `accountTable`, `eventLogTable`
- Function: `createEventLogFn`
- API: `authenticationGroup`, `signupQuery`, `loginQuery`, `meQuery`
- Types (erase at compile time — `import type` costs no bundle bytes):
  `User`, `PublicUser`, `Account`, `EventLog`, `AuthTokenResponse`,
  `RegisterAuthOptions`
- `PUBLIC_USER_FIELDS` — the runtime array `auth/me` selects; `PublicUser` is
  `Pick<User, typeof PUBLIC_USER_FIELDS[number]>`, so the two cannot drift.

## Calling the endpoints from a typed client

Every query carries its own route and payload types, so a frontend reuses the
def instead of re-typing URLs and bodies. Request types are derived; all three
responses are fully resolved — no `unknown` — `me` by derivation, `signup` and
`login` by a hand-declared `responseShape`:

```ts
// Evaluating the module that calls registerAuth is what pins the canonical;
// without it the bare getPath() below throws. Or use getPath({ canonical }).
import "./xano/index.js";
import { loginQuery, meQuery, type AuthTokenResponse } from "@sidestep/auth";
import type { InferInput, InferResponse } from "@sidestep/core";

type LoginBody = InferInput<typeof loginQuery>;      // { email?: string; password?: string }
type LoginOut  = InferResponse<typeof loginQuery>;   // AuthTokenResponse
type MeOut     = InferResponse<typeof meQuery>;      // PublicUser | null

const BASE = "https://your-instance.xano.io";

const res = await fetch(BASE + loginQuery.getPath(), {
  method: loginQuery.verb,                            // "POST"
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ email, password } satisfies LoginBody),
});
const { authToken }: LoginOut = await res.json();
```

`signup`/`login` declare `responseShape: AuthTokenResponse` because the token is
minted by a statement (opaque to the static walk); a declared shape overrides
derivation and is not cross-checked against the stack, so those two are a
hand-maintained contract. `meQuery` declares **nothing** — core derives
`PublicUser | null` from its stack, narrowing the `db.get` to the columns in
`PUBLIC_USER_FIELDS` and carrying that statement's miss-to-null. The `| null` is
the faithful-port quirk below surfacing in the type, not an oversight: callers
are forced to handle a token whose user row is gone. Do not add a
`responseShape` to `meQuery` — it would only let the declaration drift from the
`output` list.

**`getPath()` needs a canonical.** It builds `/api:<canonical>/<name>`, and by
default this package pins none (identity is the consumer's lock). A canonical
can't be minted on demand — it must be unique per instance — so a **bare
`getPath()` throws** unless one is supplied. Preferred: pin it at registration,
`registerAuth(workspace("my-app"), { canonical: "authn" })`, which makes the
deployed path and the client-derived path one value and needs no lock in the
browser (an in-code canonical beats the lock; it must match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`,
and because the group def is process-wide, once pinned every later
`registerAuth` must pass the same value — a different value *or* an omitted one
throws, rather than retargeting or being silently inherited by a workspace
registered earlier. Uniqueness across the instance's API groups is the caller's
responsibility; a collision surfaces at Xano import). Otherwise pass it per call,
`getPath({ canonical })`, or seed the lock once at startup with
`seedLockOverrides(readLockFile("./xano.lock"))` — `readLockFile` comes from the
Node-only `@sidestep/core/node` entry. Run `npx sidestep export --lock` once to
mint and freeze the canonical.

Cherry-pick individual defs instead of `registerAuth` for granular control; keep
each def's dependencies together (queries need `userTable`; `createEventLogFn`
needs `eventLogTable`). Never register a def twice.

## Constraints for agents (read before using)

- **`userTable` is this package's auth table** (`auth: true`), and `auth/me`
  names it directly (core >= 3.0.0 binds a query's `auth` to a table def, not
  `true`). A consumer may register their own additional `auth: true` table;
  these endpoints still authenticate against `user`.
- **Call `registerAuth` at most once per `Xano` instance** — it throws otherwise.
- **This is a faithful 1:1 port of Xano's quick-start template**; its quirks are
  preserved on purpose. Notably:
  - `event_log.metadata` stores the full fetched user record **including the
    password hash** on signup/login. Treat `event_log` like `user`.
  - Request history captures plaintext signup/login bodies and minted tokens.
    Turn it off in code before registering — `authenticationGroup.history =
    false` (the three queries inherit from the group). Process-wide, like
    `canonical`.
  - Every endpoint (including the `auth/me` GET) writes an `event_log` row; the
    table grows unbounded with no pruning.
  - A valid token for a deleted user → `auth/me` yields no user. Typed
    `PublicUser | null`; the runtime outcome is most likely a 500 (the stack
    drills `user.id` out of a null `db.get`), not a 200 with a null body.
  - `password` is taken as `input.text()`, never `input.password()` — the column
    hashes on write, so an input-level hash would double-hash and break
    `check_password`. Do not "tighten" it.
  - Tokens live 24h with no refresh or revocation.
- **Identity is the consumer's lock, not this package.** Commit `xano.lock` to
  keep guids and the API URL stable across re-imports.
